statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the after-effect phase (paragraph beginning "Further, from Fig. 1, when visual feedback was removed after adaptation...")
statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
statistics.admissible_reason: Within-participant effect (Episode) in the after-effect phase, not a between-group contrast of old vs young.
statistics.notes: This is the within-factor Episode effect in the ANOVA for the after-effect (no-feedback) phase; it reflects the decline of the after-effect across episodes 21-25.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the after-effect phase (same sentence)
statistics.quote: ANOVA yielded significant effects for Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01); indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group.
statistics.direction_quote: indeed a close look at Fig. 1 reveals that the after-effect declined somewhat faster in the young group
statistics.admissible_reason: Interaction term (Age × Episode), not a between-group main effect on the after-effect.
statistics.notes: The paper attributes the interaction to a faster decline of the after-effect in the young group; it does not state which group had the larger after-effect magnitude.

statistics.locator: Results, ANOVA for the after-effect phase
statistics.effect_as_written: Age (main effect) in the after-effect phase
statistics.direction_quote: the resulting after-effect was similar in both age groups
statistics.admissible_reason: No statistic printed for the Age main effect in the after-effect phase; only Episode and the interaction are reported.
statistics.notes: For the after-effect phase the text reports only Episode (F(4,88)=66.84, P<0.001) and the interaction (F(4,88)=3.95, P<0.01). No F or p value is printed for the between-factor Age in this phase; the text only says verbally that "the resulting after-effect was similar in both age groups, and gradually declined with practice; this age-independence is in marked contrast with the findings during adaptation." The Age effects that are printed (F(1,22)=7.58, P<0.05; F(1,22)=13.42, P<0.01; F(1,22)=13.78, P<0.01) belong to the adaptation phase, the refresh phase and the episode 20 vs 26 comparison respectively - different phases, not the after-effect.

statistics.admissible_reason: No standardised effect size is printed anywhere on these pages.
statistics.notes: These pages report only F and t statistics with P levels, exponential fit parameters for the adaptation curves, and mean±SD for ages and trail-making times. No d, g, eta-squared or confidence intervals are printed.

parsed.notes: The after-effect phase (episodes 21-25, no visual feedback) is analysed with one ANOVA reported in a single sentence, which prints only the within-factor Episode and the Age × Episode interaction. No between-group (Age) statistic and no group means/SDs for the after-effect are printed in the text; Fig. 1 (a figure, not transcribable text) shows the means and standard deviations. Direction between old and young for the after-effect magnitude is not stated: the paper says the after-effect was "similar in both age groups" and only that it "declined somewhat faster in the young group."
